text: This game is a good contender for best Racing game ever made. First, if you really want this game, wait for a sale, but because you should by the Race Injection Bundle. Now here's the fun part, though the game has some content to begin with, you can easily add more through moding; and boy does this game have a lot of mods. You can race any track with any car you want, if you find the mods for it. I myself have about 100 tracks, and still counting, on my computer alone. There's online but I don't really see many people there. You'll also want a controller or wheel, because using a keyboard takes a lot of the realism away due to all the assists you'll have to use to even drive in a straight line. If you're a fan of Simulation Racing Games, but have a tight budget, this is the game for you.

text: I've had this game for almost 2 years now. I have to say, for something that was made for 2007 I was very impressed. It's true the multiplayer community is pretty much dead, but my god is this game so good. It has a HUGE variety of cars that I highly doubt you will find in any other racing sim. It has very memorable music, and sound to the game. Yeah maybe it doesn't have the quality  you see in recent car games, but this game will work on any computer and it was easy to learn how to play. The learning curve isn't too steep, but it is steep enough to learn how to race and race efficiently (on max difficulty). For anyone's first time playing racing sims, I highly recommend you start with this little gem to learn the basics of race car driving simulations. This sim takes many things into consideration that even most of the modern games would never do. The camera angles, and TV shots make this game more worth while to play. The hours written on my profile for this game are wrong btw, I've played this game 2 years before I added it's game code to steam. I have around 200+ hours on it approximately. TL DR; Pros: -Huge variety of cars for a variety of diffferent racing formats -Runs on any computer -Difficulty level with the option of "training wheels" so to speak -Music (this is a true masterpiece) -Loads of Customization for both vehicles, and on tracks -Many, many, maps! -No additional purchasable content, or excessive DLC Cons: -No Multiplayer Community -No Steam Achievements -Pit Menu is glitched sometimes -Quality not compared to today's standards -Only weather is ultimately Rain/Sunny

title: rage
text: Its a shame rage wasn't more popular, I REALLY enjoyed playing it through, even though it has its problems, I recommend anyone do the same, there is a good game here waiting to be played. Good things :   -Clearly a good game engine -Game feels nice and a pleasure to play -The game design and therefore the end product seems much better than it initially seems -You are not drowned in possibilities of this open world which seems like your going back and forth for no reason...  Bad things :  -Can feel quite Linear at times -Difficulty because of gamedesign is Abysmal  - this is not a diffcult or chllenging gmae in any form!  RAGE is very shallow on the exteria, but if you give it the time, it does introduce a very wide variety of fairly intersting, (though most are not ground breaking) dynamics and makes them work quite well(which is what is so good), it is not the sort of game that strikes you as being elegant that much at all. But trust me it has has plenty of decent stuff to keep you busy and not keep you running around for hours doing nothing and getting bored. Combat is good enough, shooting  and conquering is nice on Rage, in the usual ID way (Doom, Quake etc), but from the start the variation of weapons feels like it could be better(irronically in the ID way :P), as most are similar to any other game, though, I would suggest that all players endure this , until you get the full load of weapons and multiple ammo types which much more liberty with tactics and stratgy in combat; even with your seemingly standard load-out. Whats more becuase there is a simple crafting system , it extends the weapons further and even accessories like sentry bots, whcih is pretty cool. Its clear it trys to be Borderlands and emulates the environment, but the story is actually better than Borderlands and so is the game(or at least I prefer this).  In saying that I never really liked borderlands that much... I would play this over BL any day... The story was good, and infact the usual 'you are a special kind of soldier type' in ID games is apparent on this game too, though the different kind of Post-Apocalypse scenario is quite intersting when you think about it. The main forte of the gmae is an impressive engine via ID, which makes shooting, racing and exploring a really nice experience.  It looks nice, it feels nice in all aspects. Because of this engine, the racing/driving  doesn't look shoddy(like Borderlands) and feels ok.  There was an issue at the start of the game with the handbreak that is not balanced with the first vehicles, but trust me when I say that it improves when you get your 3rd vehicle(you may have to upgrade it).  You can adapt to using the hand break in some capacity on the 2nd vehicle though... Racing, though I am not really fussed about racing games, is not too bad, I enjoyed it.  There is plenty of variation in racing matches, from standard racing matches to the sequential  'Domination' matches(the first to get to a check point get points, the first to 40 points wins(Blowing others up gives you points too...) which does throw the strategy to race on its head(which I think is quite good). The Music is fine, parts of it sounds un-natural to me, and some of the style of both the composer and the music suck, *To me*.  But in saying that, its not too bad and the music is good when you are playing through the game, and can actually be quite good in parts. I will add the worst thing about this game was the difficulty.  This game is SSOOoo easy!  If you are bad at FPS: PLAY RAGE!  You have at least 2 lives and you heal constantly, so unless you keep passing out on the keyboard, you will be fine!  I played this on Hard and found it not much of a challenge at all and perhaps after some days that was nice, but I want a challenge from any game I play and Believe me , RAGE isn't challeging in the slightest!  I am keen to play through in nightmare mode , just to see if they actually have ANY challenging difficulty modes at all! Word of advice: If you are buying this on steam, Dont play on 64bit mode unless you have to: i.e. this mode:		* Rage 64bit(not supported) for mods* When you start up the game.  If you want to stick in the hours to finish the campaign and you want to play to get achievements, dont play on 64bit mode, also 64 bit mode takes a LONG time to load an area, and its not like 2x the time, but more like 50x.. literally my computer takes 5minutes just to load town or the wasteland from any loacation... In standard 32 bit mode, it takes about 10 seconds... So avoid 64bit mode unlesss you really want to use it!  I got half way through the game before realising achievements were not logged and had to start again on the 32bit mode ( you cant access 64bit data in 32 bit game!) .

text: Don't be fooled by all the negative reviews comparing this game to whatever other post-apocalyptic shooter and open-world game. Even though it might look like it is open-world from the screenshots, it's not. And this is a good thing! Depending on the player I guess. For me, I had no intention into investing hours and hours on exploring every nook and cranny of the wasteland in order to find hidden items and side quests. This is where I found the game to be just right. It's quite linear actually. There is no punishnment for not exploring nor an OP reward for doing so. This way you won't have to feel bad that you might have missed something which could have made the combat easier for example. Other than this you can entertain yourself with a handful of side quests which just yield you more money, which in the end you end up spending on a few (but not necessary) upgrade items but mostly just ammo. There are racing and slaughter mini games on which you can spend more time which yield, once again, just more money or upgrades for your vehicles. Be warned though! Driving in this game is quite bad. The controls are hard and the cars pretty much drive like air. It can get somewhat annoying in certain racing modes, but once you eventually master the♥♥♥♥♥controls, you're fine. What was surprising to me is how short the game felt and how unsatisfying the ending was. Mind you, there are no bosses in particular. Except maybe slightly more armored enemies but that's it. At the end, there is no ominous boss fight which cumlinates in you saving the world or whatever... no. You just fight of hordes (although you can't even call them proper hordes) of enemies, walk up to a terminal and push the button. That's it. Yup. The final fight is just unloading all your carefully hoarded ammo into some 20-30 enemies and using a terminal. Congrats you finished the game! Despite the ending being just plain balls, I liked most of the gameplay leading up to it. The characters were also interesting. They aren't particularly deeply portrayed but you can certainly get into some funny conversations with random personas which you meet around town. There's a ton of achivements on which you can spend extra hours if you're into that. Had some troubles with graphics though. Despite being able to run other comparable games on high with no lag, I had to find some workarounds for this one. Seems like it helps if you actually start the game as administrator and disabling the motion blur does wonders.

title: rage
text: Rage is a post-apocalyptic first person shooter with some Mad Max-style vehicle combat. The shooting is satisfying, the weapons are great - almost every weapon has some alternate ammo/fire mode, which is great fun to use. For example, the crossbow has electric bolts, the shotgun has exploding shots, or the rocket launcher has homing rockets. All weapons are useful in certain situations. You can craft a lot of things, including bandages, ammo, power-ups and robots for your aid. You have 4 quick-use slots, where you can assign anything usable you want. Unfortunately the quick-slot limit for the weapons is also 4, so if you want to use another gun, you have to reassign something. It's quite uncomfortable to use, I'd have rather seen a weapon selection wheel. There are towns, where you can talk to people, buy/sell stuff, try some minigames, get side-missions, and participate in races. The races are needed to earn race certificates to upgrade your vehicle. The racing is simple, but fun. In the Wasteland you can show the bandits your new vehicle upgrades and weapons, and blow them up to oblivion. Quite satisfying. The graphics are a mixed bag, the characters look great, and the environments are looking good too, but only in a distance. If you look closer, everything is a blurry mess (even with forced 16K textures). I have a powerful PC for a 2011 game, and I needed tweaks to eliminate the horrible texture pop-in. The story is quite basic, but the ending is downright insulting: you expect a big boss fight, even the NPCs are mentioning it, but you get NOTHING. Nada. It's very disappointing. Aside from the crappy ending, I really enjoyed this game, so I wholeheartedly recommend to any FPS fan.

text: "Welcome to the wasteland son. It's pretty ugly out here. I need you to do something for me. We've lost communications with the scouts at the northern outpost. We need medical supplies from them but fear something has happened. Can you please go and check out what's happened to them" And so - after stocking up on supplies and ammunition - you leave the safe haven of the settler settlement and head north towards adventure ...for about 10 seconds. Are you kidding me old man? The Northern outpost is about 200 yards away. You could find out what's happened to the scouts with a good pair of binoculars. Oh btw they're dead and you will have to fight 38 mutants, but that's the fun bit. RAGE is a game that's all about scale. It has everything a good open world game has. Wastelands, Cities (well, 2 of them anyway), crafting, side-quests, races, a smash-TV style battle arena, stunt jumps, delivery jobs, gambling mini-games, a really awesome trading card game, and more. And it fits all of this into a match box. This is the smallest "open world" you'll ever see. I swear that everything is within a minute distance of everything else. It's both ridiculous and amazing. For the rest, it's pretty fun, the game doesn't take itself too seriously - I think there was a story but it's not that important - the combat plays a bit like borderlands minus the loot but with a nice variety of weapons, ammo, and sentrybots, and all in all it's definitely worth a playthrough. The game ends like it started: abruptly, not far from the start, and without getting boring.
